attribution.note: Marcus's own Substack post. It is a joint essay with Schroeder and Kunst, but Marcus published it under his name as a co-author, so he endorses the sentence.

semantics.note: The draft faithfully restates the second clause as a past observation. The first clause, that bots were a problem since early social media, is a separate point and is fairly left out.

contract.note: The speaker gave no measure for 'quick'. Reading it as documented use within one to two years of ChatGPT's release is an ordinary plain reading. The evidence meets it well inside that window, so the result does not depend on how 'quick' is read.

evidence.note: AFP report, May 2024, on OpenAI's disclosure. Five state-linked and commercial influence operations used OpenAI models to write comments and articles, about 18 months after ChatGPT launched. It relays a company disclosure, but AFP is a reputable outlet.

FBI statements from July 2024 describe a generative-AI-enhanced Russian bot farm used for AI-generated disinformation, with access dating to 2022. The contract's support condition also counts generative AI, though the item does not specifically say the tool was an LLM.

Anthropic threat report published April 2025. It documents an influence-as-a-service operation using Claude to generate content and run bot accounts. This is a company disclosure, but the contract allows AI company threat reports, and it backs up e1.

reviews.rationale: Several credible dated reports from 2024 and 2025 (OpenAI via AFP, FBI/DOJ, Anthropic) show state and commercial influence operations using LLMs to generate disinformation within about 18 months of LLMs becoming widely available. That meets the plain-reading support condition. e1 says the campaigns gained little audience, but that bears on their impact, not on whether they adopted LLMs. The packet contains no counterevidence.
